name: Buffer Underwrite ('Buffer Underflow')
principle: The product writes through an index or pointer that can refer before the start of a buffer. This corrupts adjacent memory and can cause crashes, policy bypass, or code execution.
detection_signals: buf[index] = value where index is decremented and no index >= 0 check dominates the write
while/for loop writes buf[len] then executes len-- without len >= 0 or pointer >= buf guard
char *p = strstr(buf, needle); int idx = p - buf; write to &buf[idx] without p != NULL check
strcpy(&buf[idx], src) or memcpy(&buf[idx], src, n) where idx is signed and may be negative
pointer write through *p or p[i] after p-- or p -= n without p >= buf check
size/length arithmetic result is cast between signed and unsigned then used as destination offset before buffer
negative_signals: write guarded by index >= 0 && index < size before buf[index]
backward scan loop condition includes len >= 0 before every buf[len] write
pointer destination guarded by p >= buf && p < buf + size before write
strstr/memchr/find result checked for NULL or npos before pointer subtraction or indexing
destination offset type and validation prevent negative values before memcpy/strcpy/memmove
false_defense_traps: checking only index < size but not index >= 0
checking only upper buffer overflow while backward traversal can cross the lower bound
using strstr result in pointer arithmetic before checking for NULL
assuming empty or all-whitespace input cannot drive a decrement loop below zero
treating all buffer underflow reports as reads; CWE-124 requires a write
verification_focus: Can any write destination index or pointer evaluate to an address before the buffer start?

consequence_chains.trigger: range check omits the minimum bound and a negative index reaches a write
consequence_chains.consequence: memory before the buffer is overwritten
memory corruption, crash, or controlled code execution

patch_principle: Validate every computed index or pointer against the lower and upper buffer bounds before writing.
Add lower-bound termination checks to backward scans and decrement loops.
Check search results such as strstr or memchr for NULL before pointer arithmetic.
Use size_t or bounded abstractions carefully; do not cast negative signed offsets to unsigned.
Prefer memory-safe APIs or languages with automatic bounds checks.

minimal_examples.vuln: char *p = strstr(destBuf, "Replace Me"); int idx = p - destBuf; strcpy(&destBuf[idx], srcBuf);
minimal_examples.safe: char *p = strstr(destBuf, "Replace Me"); if (p != NULL) strcpy(p, srcBuf);
